Grayscale Says Zcash's 20% Developer Funding Has Fueled a Decade of Innovation Grayscale, a leading digital asset manager, highlighted Zcash's (ZEC) continued innovation ahead of its 10th anniversary on October 28, attributing part of its progress to the allocation of 20% of block rewards to developer funding. The privacy-focused cryptocurrency has evolved through multiple shielded pools, from Sprout and Sapling to Orchard and the 2026 Ironwood upgrade, which introduced quantum-recoverable addresses and formal verification to address security vulnerabilities. — link

Zcash Co-Founder Proposes Redirecting 8% of Block Subsidies to Network Sustainability Mechanism Zcash co-founder and protocol developer Sean Bowe has submitted a draft Zcash Improvement Proposal (ZIP) to end the 8% block subsidy allocation to Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) and redirect it to the Network Sustainability Mechanism (NSM), withholding the funds from immediate circulation. The proposal argues that ZCG's existing reserves are sufficient to sustain its grant-making activities. It would leave ZCG's existing treasury, the separate 12% Coinholder-Controlled Fund allocation, miners' subsidy share, and ZEC's maximum supply unchanged. — link

Bitcoin ETFs Draw $110 Million as Ether Funds Shed $88.6 Million According to SoSoValue, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $110 million in net inflows on October 26, entirely driven by BlackRock's IBIT, bringing its cumulative net inflows to $66.24 billion. Spot Ethereum ETFs saw $88.58 million in net outflows, although Fidelity's FETH led individual fund inflows with $16.13 million. BlackRock is the world's largest asset manager, while Fidelity is one of the largest U.S. investment firms. — link

Binance Files for Brazilian Crypto License Ahead of October 30 Deadline; Restricts 8 Services and Delists 22 Tokens in Brazil Binance filed an application with Brazil’s central bank on October 23 through its local entity BBrasil to operate as a virtual asset service provider (SPSAV), ahead of the October 30 regulatory deadline, according to Blocknews. To comply with local rules, Binance began restricting eight services for Brazilian users on October 27, including crypto loans, margin trading, mining pools and cloud mining, while delisting 22 tokens, including USDE, USTC, DCR and XVG. Existing positions in affected products are generally limited to reductions or closures, with new positions prohibited. Binance also plans to complete the migration of Brazilian users to its local payment-account structure by October 29. — link
